title: World Cup 2026 betting pool
summary: A Mexican app expects 2 million players during the 2026 World Cup matches, and bets spike at minute 90.

requirements.1: {{s1}} is the HTTP proxy that receives bets over HTTPS, spreads the requests across the containers and passes the player's IP to the API in the X-Forwarded-For header.
requirements.2: {{s2}} runs the API in containers without the two-person team managing servers, nodes or a Kubernetes cluster.
requirements.3: {{s3}} keeps the leaderboard of 2 million players in memory, sorted by points, so the API does not hit the database on every lookup.
requirements.4: {{s4}} absorbs the minute-90 spike: workers pull bets at their own pace and each one is done only when they confirm they processed it; otherwise it is delivered again.
requirements.5: {{s5}} is the NoSQL store for the bets: it saves each one keyed by player and match and writes it only if that key does not exist yet, so nobody bets twice.
requirements.6: The score provider sends each goal to the slot 2 API, which updates the slot 3 leaderboard.

s1.explanation: Application Gateway works at layer 7 and can sit in front of Container Apps in an internal environment integrated with the virtual network; it adds the x-forwarded-for header with the player's IP and port.

s2.explanation: Azure Container Apps is a serverless platform for containers: the team does not configure servers or orchestrate containers, and apps scale on HTTP traffic or events.
s2.hint_cue: without the two-person team managing servers

s3.explanation: Azure Managed Redis is an in-memory data store that builds leaderboards with the sorted set structure, and Redis is typically much faster than a relational database.

s4.explanation: In a Service Bus queue several workers read and each message is processed by only one. In peek lock mode the message is locked; if it is not completed before the lock expires, Service Bus delivers it again.

s5.explanation: In Azure Cosmos DB each item has an id that is unique within its logical partition, and creating a document with an id already taken returns 409 Conflict. Writes take less than 10 ms at the 99th percentile.
s5.hint_cue: writes it only if that key does not exist yet

azure-load-balancer.s1: Azure Load Balancer spreads layer 4 TCP or UDP traffic, and its IP-based backend pool only accepts virtual machines or scale sets, not other PaaS services such as Container Apps.

azure-aks.s2: AKS is a Kubernetes cluster, which the requirement rules out, and in AKS Standard the team creates and manages the node pools by hand.

azure-mysql-read-replica.s3: A MySQL read replica is another copy of the relational database, and the Azure Managed Redis guide explains that Redis is typically much faster than a relational database.
azure-mysql-read-replica.s5: MySQL read replicas are read-only, so they cannot take the write of each bet.

azure-event-hubs.s4: In Event Hubs the consumer stores its own checkpoints and events cannot be deleted explicitly; the requirement asks to confirm each bet one by one.

azure-blob-storage.s5: Blob Storage is optimized for storing massive amounts of unstructured data; the requirement asks for a NoSQL database.
